topics.title: Appendix D — Capstone acceptance worksheet
topics.summary: Use this worksheet after completing Chapter 20. Fill it with observed evidence from your own build, not the publishing environment’s results copied without qualification.

cards.question: What distinguishes an acceptance worksheet from a list of intentions?
cards.answer: Each requirement names a test, an observed result, and evidence. A check mark without a witness does not prove the feature works.

cards.question: Why should the capstone include an empty-input case?
cards.answer: It tests startup and termination without normal commands. The program needs a defined result rather than assuming every session contains useful input.

cards.question: Why test a failed command followed by a successful one?
cards.answer: The sequence checks recovery and preserved state. Separate runs can miss failure state that corrupts later commands.

cards.question: What should a final acceptance review say about missing checks?
cards.answer: Identify the missing evidence explicitly. Do not report complete acceptance merely because the available happy-path demonstrations passed.

cards.question: What must bool acceptanceComplete(const std::vector<bool>& checks) accept and reject?
cards.answer: Return true only when at least one required check was supplied and every supplied result is true. An empty list is incomplete, not proof of acceptance. This models recorded checks; it does not execute the application tests.

cards.question: Predict the output: Do not accept an empty checklist. Assume the required standard-library headers; the function and sample main are shown.
cards.answer:
false
Why: A nonempty check makes the evidence requirement explicit before a simple all-results scan.

cards.question: What is wrong with this starter for Do not accept an empty checklist?
cards.answer: The starter returns true for an empty vector. The loop has no failing result, but the contract also requires actual evidence. Repair: Success means evidence exists and every supplied required check passed. It does not assert that unlisted requirements were tested.

cards.question: What must stay true while implementing Do not accept an empty checklist?
cards.answer: Success means evidence exists and every supplied required check passed. It does not assert that unlisted requirements were tested.

cards.question: Why was this design selected for Do not accept an empty checklist?
cards.answer: A nonempty check makes the evidence requirement explicit before a simple all-results scan.

cards.question: Which competing design could solve Do not accept an empty checklist, and when is it useful?
cards.answer: A report with named requirements and missing-result states is stronger for a real release. This Boolean summary is a small exercise about the acceptance boundary.

focus.title: Do not accept an empty checklist

Evaluate this condition before continuing. A true guard takes its return or throw path; && requires both conditions, while || accepts either.
The colon separates the element declaration from its range. A plain value copies each element; & borrows it, and const prevents writes through that borrow.
